title: Unit 07: Parts of Speech: Nouns, Pronouns, Adjectives & Adverbs
subject: english-10

questions.question: Identify the type of noun: 'His *eloquence* mesmerized the audience.'
questions.explanation: 'Eloquence' refers to an intangible quality or abstract faculty of fluent, persuasive speech, making it an Abstract Noun.

questions.question: Identify the type of noun: 'A *flock* of migratory birds flew over the lake.'
questions.explanation: 'Flock' designates a group or collection of birds regarded as a unified entity, defining a Collective Noun.

questions.question: Choose the correct irregular plural of 'criterion':
questions.explanation: 'Criterion' originates from Greek, and its standard plural form in academic English is 'criteria'.

questions.question: Choose the correct plural form of the foreign biological term 'cactus':
questions.explanation: 'Cactus' derives from Latin, forming its traditional classical plural as 'cacti'.

questions.question: Identify the type of pronoun: 'He *himself* admitted his fault before the magistrate.'
questions.explanation: 'Himself' placed directly after the subject 'He' is used solely to add dramatic emphasis, making it an Emphatic (Intensive) pronoun.

questions.question: Identify the type of pronoun: 'The careless skater injured *himself* on the ice.'
questions.explanation: Here the action of the verb 'injured' reflects back upon the subject 'skater', serving as direct object and functioning as a Reflexive Pronoun.

questions.question: Identify the type of adjective: 'Abdullah won the *second* prize in the debate.'
questions.explanation: 'Second' indicates position in a series/order, which classifies it as an Ordinal Numeral Adjective (compared to cardinals like one, two, three).

questions.question: Identify the type of adjective: 'There is *little* hope of his recovery.'
questions.explanation: 'Little' modifies the uncountable abstract noun 'hope' by showing amount/quantity, making it an Adjective of Quantity.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative form: 'Mount Everest is ___ than any other peak on Earth.'
questions.explanation: Comparison between two entities ('Mount Everest' vs 'any other peak') signaled by 'than' requires the comparative degree 'higher'.

questions.question: Identify the underlined adverb: 'She arrived *lately*.' What does 'lately' mean here?
questions.explanation: The adverb 'lately' means 'recently' or 'in recent times', distinct from the adverb 'late' which means 'after the scheduled time'.

questions.question: Which sentence follows the conventional ORDER OF ADJECTIVES (Opinion - Size - Age - Color - Origin - Material)?

options.A: She bought a lovely, small, ancient, wooden box.
options.B: She bought an ancient, wooden, small, lovely box.
options.C: She bought a wooden, ancient, lovely, small box.
options.D: She bought a small, wooden, ancient, lovely box.

questions.explanation: The natural royal order of adjectives places Opinion ('lovely') before Size ('small'), Age ('ancient'), and Material ('wooden').

questions.question: Identify the type of pronoun: 'The boy *whose* bicycle was stolen lodged a complaint.'
questions.explanation: 'Whose' shows possession and connects the subordinate clause to the antecedent noun 'The boy', qualifying as a Possessive Relative Pronoun.

questions.question: Identify the underlined word: 'The horse ran *fast*.' 'Fast' is an:
questions.explanation: 'Fast' answers 'How did the horse run?' modifying the verb 'ran', which makes it an Adverb of Manner.

questions.question: Identify the underlined word: 'He is a *fast* runner.' 'Fast' is an:
questions.explanation: Here 'fast' directly modifies the noun 'runner', functioning as an Adjective.

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'Between you and ___, there should be no misunderstandings.'
questions.explanation: 'Between' is a preposition, and prepositions strictly govern objective case pronouns ('between you and me', not 'between you and I').

questions.question: Identify the type of noun: 'The *furniture* in the hall is imported from Italy.'
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun that cannot be pluralized with '-s' and always takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Choose the correct irregular plural form of 'phenomenon':
questions.explanation: 'Phenomenon' has a Greek origin and changes to 'phenomena' in the plural.

questions.question: Identify the type of pronoun: '*These* are the books recommended by the instructor.'
questions.explanation: 'These' stands alone as the subject replacing the noun phrase, making it a Demonstrative Pronoun.

questions.question: Identify the type of word: '*These* books belong to the library.' 'These' is a:
questions.explanation: When 'these' immediately precedes and modifies the noun 'books', it functions as a Demonstrative Adjective.

questions.question: Identify the reciprocal pronoun in the following sentence: 'The two rivals congratulated *each other*.'
questions.explanation: 'Each other' is a Reciprocal Pronoun used when two entities mutually interact (in contrast to 'one another' for three or more).

questions.question: Choose the correct superlative form: 'Of all the candidates, he gave the ___ presentation.'
questions.explanation: When comparing more than two items, the superlative degree of 'good' is 'best'.

questions.question: Identify the adverb of FREQUENCY: 'He *seldom* makes errors in calculations.'
questions.explanation: 'Seldom' tells how often an action happens, functioning as an Adverb of Frequency.

questions.question: Identify the type of adjective: 'Which path should we take?' 'Which' is an:
questions.explanation: 'Which' modifies the noun 'path' to form a question, making it an Interrogative Adjective.

questions.question: Choose the correct irregular plural of 'crisis':
questions.explanation: Nouns of Greek origin ending in '-is' form their plural by changing '-is' to '-es' ('crisis' -> 'crises').

questions.question: Identify the type of adverb: 'The weather is *extremely* cold today.'
questions.explanation: 'Extremely' modifies the adjective 'cold' by showing its intensity or level, qualifying as an Adverb of Degree.

questions.question: Identify the type of pronoun: '*Everyone* must sign the attendance register.'
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' refers to persons generally without specifying particular individuals, classifying as an Indefinite Pronoun.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence regarding degrees of comparison:

options.A: Karachi is bigger than any other city in Pakistan.
options.B: Karachi is bigger than any city in Pakistan.
options.C: Karachi is the most biggest city in Pakistan.
options.D: Karachi is more bigger than Lahore.

questions.explanation: In comparative constructions comparing a city with other members of its own group, 'any other' is required to prevent illogical self-comparison.

questions.question: Identify the collective noun denoting ships:
questions.explanation: The authentic collective noun for naval or commercial vessels is a 'fleet'.

questions.question: Identify the underlined word: 'This is the *very* book I was searching for.' 'Very' is an:
questions.explanation: When 'very' directly modifies a noun ('book') to mean 'exact/same', it functions as an Emphasizing Adjective.

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'One must be faithful to ___ country.'
questions.explanation: The indefinite pronoun 'one' must maintain pronoun consistency with 'one's' (not 'his' or 'their').

questions.question: Identify the type of adverb: 'The injured player walked *slowly* off the pitch.'
questions.explanation: 'Slowly' answers 'How did he walk?' classifying it as an Adverb of Manner.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative: 'This book is ___ to that one.'
questions.explanation: Latin comparatives ending in '-ior' (superior, inferior, senior, junior, prior) take the preposition 'to' and never take 'more' or 'than'.

questions.question: Identify the abstract noun derived from the adjective 'brave':
questions.explanation: 'Bravery' is the abstract noun; 'bravely' is an adverb, while 'braver/bravest' are degrees of comparison.

questions.question: Identify the type of pronoun: '*Whom* did the committee appoint as chairman?'
questions.explanation: 'Whom' functions as the objective interrogative pronoun receiving the action of the verb 'appoint'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence containing an ADVERB OF PLACE:

options.A: The children played outside all afternoon.

questions.explanation: 'Outside' indicates the spatial location/direction where the action occurred, functioning as an Adverb of Place.
